name: Cox's Bazar
shortDescription: The world's longest natural sandy sea beach, stretching over 120 km along the Bay of Bengal.
recommendedActivities: Sunset cruise on the Bay of Bengal
location: Kolatoli, Cox's Bazar Sadar, Cox's Bazar, Chattogram, Bangladesh

name: Sajek Valley
shortDescription: A scenic hill valley at the top of the Tripura mountains, famous for clouds floating below the peaks.
recommendedActivities: Watch the sunrise over cloud valleys

name: Bandarban
shortDescription: The hill-district capital surrounded by green hills, waterfalls and indigenous culture.

name: Rangamati
shortDescription: A lake-town on the shores of Kaptai Lake, known for the indigenous Chakma culture and floating markets.
recommendedActivities: Visit Hanging Bridge over the lake

name: Sylhet
shortDescription: The tea capital of Bangladesh with lush tea gardens, waterfalls and tranquil haors.
recommendedActivities: Visit the 201-step Shah Jalal shrine area

name: Sreemangal
shortDescription: Known as the tea capital of Bangladesh, home to endless tea estates and the Lawachara rainforest.

name: Saint Martin's Island
shortDescription: Bangladesh's only coral island in the Bay of Bengal, with crystal-clear water and white sand beaches.
location: Saint Martin's Island, Teknaf, Cox's Bazar, Chattogram, Bangladesh

name: Kuakata
shortDescription: A rare beach where you can watch both sunrise and sunset over the sea, known as the 'Sagor Kannya'.
recommendedActivities: Watch sunrise and sunset on the same beach
Walking along the golden sandy shore
Fresh coconut water by the sea

name: Jaflong
shortDescription: A hill-side village beside the Piyain river where stone collecting and scenic river views meet the border hills.
recommendedActivities: Boat ride on the Piyain river
Views of the Dawki border hills

name: Ratargul
shortDescription: A freshwater swamp forest, the Amazon of Bangladesh, where trees rise straight out of the water.
recommendedActivities: Boat ride through the submerged forest

name: Tanguar Haor
shortDescription: A UNESCO Ramsar wetland in Sunamganj that becomes a vast inland sea during the monsoon.

name: Nafakhum
shortDescription: The 'Niagara of Bangladesh', a dramatic waterfall on the Remakri river in Thanchi, Bandarban.
recommendedActivities: Trek through the Remakri river valley

name: Kaptai
shortDescription: Gateway to the artificial Kaptai Lake, Bangladesh's largest man-made lake surrounded by hills.

name: Patenga
shortDescription: A popular urban beach near Chattogram port where the river meets the Bay of Bengal.
recommendedActivities: Evening stroll on the sea wall
Watch ships in the port channel
Sunset over the Bay of Bengal

name: Sonargaon
shortDescription: The ancient capital of Bengal, home to the folk museum 'Panam City' and centuries-old monuments.
recommendedActivities: Visit the Folk Art & Crafts Museum

name: Madhabkunda
shortDescription: The largest waterfall in Bangladesh, plunging through layers of green forest in Moulvibazar.

name: Paharpur
shortDescription: Home to Somapura Mahavihara, the largest Buddhist monastery ruins in South Asia and a UNESCO World Heritage site.
recommendedActivities: Sunset view from the stupa terrace

name: Bagerhat
shortDescription: A UNESCO city of mosques, home to the magnificent Sixty Dome Mosque of Khan Jahan Ali.
recommendedActivities: Boat ride on the Ghora Dighi lake

name: Chattogram
shortDescription: The major commercial port city of Bangladesh, known as the gateway to the Bay of Bengal.

name: Patenga Beach
shortDescription: A popular urban beach near Chattogram port where the river meets the Bay of Bengal.
recommendedActivities: Evening stroll on the sea wall
Watch ships in the port channel
Sunset over the Bay of Bengal

name: Foy's Lake
shortDescription: A scenic man-made lake in Chattogram, popular for boating and amusement parks.

name: Batali Hill
shortDescription: The highest hill in Chattogram city, offering panoramic views of the city and surrounding areas.

name: Chattogram War Cemetery
shortDescription: A Commonwealth War Cemetery maintaining the graves of Allied soldiers who died in World War II.
recommendedActivities: Pay respects at the war graves

name: Ethnological Museum
shortDescription: Bangladesh's only ethnological museum, displaying the cultures of the country's diverse tribal groups.

name: Chattogram Zoo
shortDescription: A zoological garden in Chattogram featuring local and exotic animals.
location: Foy's Lake Area, Khulshi, Chattogram, Bangladesh

name: Sitakunda
shortDescription: A upazila town in Chattogram division known for its hills, rivers and religious sites.

name: Chandranath Hill
shortDescription: A sacred hill in the Chattogram Hill Tracts, home to a Hindu temple at the summit.
recommendedActivities: Hike to the temple at the summit

name: Guliakhali Beach
shortDescription: A quiet beach in Chattogram district known for its clean sand and fishing villages.

name: Bashbaria Beach
shortDescription: A scenic beach in Chattogram area with coconut groves and less commercialization.
recommendedActivities: Beach walking and coconut grove views

name: Khoiyachora Waterfall
shortDescription: A beautiful waterfall in Fatikchhari upazila, Chattogram division, within hiking distance from nearby villages.

name: Naphittachora Waterfall
shortDescription: A scenic waterfall in Fatikchhari upazila, less visited and relatively pristine.

name: Mohamaya Lake
shortDescription: A serene lake in Chattogram district, surrounded by greenery and local villages.

name: Bhatiari
shortDescription: An upazila in Chattogram division known for its river systems and natural beauty.

name: Mirsarai
shortDescription: An upazila in Chattogram division with coastal areas, hills and agricultural lands.

name: Lalbagh Fort
shortDescription: Mughal fort complex built in 1678, featuring the tomb of Pari Bibi, audience hall, and mosque along the Buriganga river.

name: Ahsan Manzil
shortDescription: Pink palace of the Nawab of Dhaka, situated on the banks of Buriganga River, now a museum of colonial architecture.

name: Faridpur Museum
shortDescription: District museum showcasing artifacts, portraits and historical items from Faridpur's rich medieval and colonial past.

name: Bangabandhu Safari Park
shortDescription: Bangladesh's first wildlife safari park, home to deer, elephants, birds and botanical gardens in Kashimpur, Gazipur.

name: Chandra Area
shortDescription: Historic riverine area of Chandra upazila, known for its bamboo groves, river banks and traditional boat building.

name: Bangabandhu Mausoleum, Tungipara
shortDescription: Mausoleum of Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman in his hometown Tungipara, Gopalganj, featuring his personal belongings and memorial.

name: Bajrajogini Temple
shortDescription: Ancient Hindu temple of Bajrajogini on the banks of Kangsha River, dating back to the medieval period, highly revered locally.

name: Manikganj Char Rajbari
shortDescription: Ruins of a 19th-century palace on a river char (sandbank) in Manikganj, overlooking the Padma River, reflecting colonial-era architecture.

name: Chandradighi
shortDescription: Archaeological site of the ancient Chandradighi kingdom capital, featuring ruins of old palaces, temples and city walls from the Bengal Sultanate period.

name: Armenian Church
shortDescription: The Armenian Church of the Holy Resurrection, built in 1781, is a rare example of colonial Christian architecture in Narayanganj's old city area.

name: Ashuganj Port
shortDescription: Major river port on the Meghna River at Ashuganj, Brahmanbaria, key hub for cargo vessels and river steamers connecting Dhaka with eastern and northern Bangladesh.

name: Narsingdi Museum
shortDescription: District museum displaying archaeological artifacts, folk heritage, portraits of freedom fighters and items from Narsingdi's riverine civilization.

name: Rajbari Rajbari
shortDescription: Historic palace complex of the Rajbari district, featuring colonial-era buildings, audience halls and landscaped gardens along the Padma River.

name: Shariatpur Char Area
shortDescription: River char (sandbank) landscape in Shariatpur on the Padma River, known for fishing villages, river biodiversity and rural char life.

name: Modhupur Forest
shortDescription: Sal forest area spanning Tangail and Gazipur, home to deer, primates, birds and indigenous communities, offering eco-trekking and nature trails.

name: Gouripur Heritage
shortDescription: Ancestral village of Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman at Gouripur, Tangail, featuring historic sites, memorial complex and rural Bengal heritage.

name: National Parliament House
shortDescription: The Jatiya Sangsad Bhaban, designed by architect Louis Kahn, is one of the world's largest legislative complexes and an icon of modernist architecture in Sher-e-Bangla Nagar, Dhaka.

name: Bangladesh National Museum
shortDescription: The largest museum in Bangladesh, housing archaeological artifacts, art, history and natural history galleries in Shahbag, Dhaka.

name: Star Mosque
shortDescription: An 18th-century Mughal-style mosque in Old Dhaka, renowned for its walls adorned with thousands of hand-painted blue star tiles.

name: Dhakeshwari Temple
shortDescription: The national temple of Bangladesh and the oldest Hindu temple in Dhaka, built in the 12th century and dedicated to Goddess Dhakeshwari.

name: National Martyrs' Memorial
shortDescription: A 46-metre monument in Savar honouring the martyrs of the 1971 Liberation War, designed by Syed Mainul Hossain, with seven ascending concrete towers.

name: Ramna Park
shortDescription: The largest and greenest park in central Dhaka, surrounding the Ramna Lake, popular for morning walks, jogging and boating in the heart of the city.

name: Mathurapur Deul
shortDescription: A 16th-century terracotta-decorated Hindu temple tower in Faridpur, one of the finest surviving examples of Bengal's Deul temple architecture.

name: Pathrail Mosque
shortDescription: A Sultanate-era mosque in Faridpur dating from the late 15th century, noted for its terracotta ornamentation and single-domed Bengal style.

name: Bhawal National Park
shortDescription: A 5,022-acre sal forest in Gazipur, one of Bangladesh's first national parks, home to deer, monkeys, birds and a central lake, popular for nature trails and picnics.

name: Nuhash Polli
shortDescription: The scenic riverside home and estate of legendary writer Humayun Ahmed in Gazipur, set among trees on the Turag river, open to visitors as a literary landmark.

name: Bhawal Rajbari
shortDescription: The grand 19th-century palace of the Bhawal zamindari estate in Joydebpur, Gazipur, a vast colonial-era building reflecting the estate's former opulence.

name: Ulpur Zamindar Bari
shortDescription: A 19th-century zamindar mansion at Ulpur in Gopalganj, known for its terracotta work, traditional Bengal architecture and historical significance.

name: Orakandi Thakur Bari
shortDescription: The ancestral home of the Fakir and Baul Lalon families at Orakandi, Gopalganj, a revered site associated with folk spirituality and the Baul tradition.

name: Nikli Haor
shortDescription: A vast seasonal wetland in Kishoreganj that floods into a huge inland sea during the monsoon, drawing migratory birds in winter and offering houseboat journeys.

name: Mithamain Haor
shortDescription: One of Bangladesh's largest haors in Mithamain, Kishoreganj, famous for its monsoon water expanse, floating villages and the annual Mithamain fish festival.

name: Sholakia Eidgah
shortDescription: A historic 19th-century open-air Eidgah in Kishoreganj town, one of the largest congregation grounds in South Asia where Eid prayers gather tens of thousands.

name: Jangalbari Fort
shortDescription: Ruins of a 16th-century fort at Jangalbari in Kishoreganj, associated with the Baro-Bhuyan rulers, featuring a massive earthen mound and old gateway.

name: Pagla Mosque
shortDescription: A late-19th-century ornate mosque in Kishoreganj town, renowned for its elaborate domes, arches and terracotta details, a striking example of Mughal revival style.

name: Raja Ram Temple
shortDescription: A historic Hindu temple at Tekerhat in Madaripur, known for its terracotta panels and regional Bengal temple architecture.

name: Shakuni Dighi
shortDescription: A large historic water tank in Madaripur town, once a major source of drinking water, now a scenic lake surrounded by trees and walkways.

name: Kalikhola Zamindar Bari
shortDescription: A 19th-century zamindar mansion at Kalikhola in Madaripur, exhibiting colonial-era architecture and terracotta ornamentation of Bengal's landed gentry.

name: Baliati Zamindar Bari
shortDescription: A magnificent complex of seven zamindari palaces at Baliati in Manikganj, one of the largest estate houses in Bangladesh with over 200 rooms and ornate interiors.

name: Aricha Ghat
shortDescription: A busy ferry ghat on the Padma river in Manikganj, where launches and ferries connect the capital with southwestern Bangladesh, offering sweeping river views.

name: Baba Adam Mosque
shortDescription: A 15th-century Sultanate mosque at Rampal in Munshiganj, decorated with fine terracotta panels and carved stone, a protected archaeological monument.

name: Idrakpur Fort
shortDescription: A 17th-century Mughal river fort near Munshiganj town, built to guard the waterways to Dhaka, with octagonal bastions and massive ramparts.

name: Sonarang Twin Temples
shortDescription: A pair of 17th-century terracotta Hindu temples at Sonarang in Munshiganj, noted for their ribbed domes and elaborate decorative brickwork.

name: Arial Beel
shortDescription: A vast low-lying wetland in Munshiganj that becomes a huge seasonal lake during the monsoon, home to diverse birds and traditional fishing villages.

name: Goaldi Mosque
shortDescription: A 1519 Sultanate-era mosque in Sonargaon, Narayanganj, one of the finest surviving monuments of pre-Mughal Bengal with a single dome and terracotta work.

name: Hajiganj Fort
shortDescription: A 17th-century Mughal fort in Narayanganj on the banks of the Shitalakshya river, built to guard the river route to Dhaka, with strong bastions and a large gate.

name: Sonakanda Fort
shortDescription: A Mughal riverside fort in Sonakanda, Narayanganj, one of three forts built in the area to defend the waterways leading to the old capital of Dhaka.

name: Wari-Bateshwar
shortDescription: An archaeological site in Narsingdi with ancient fortifications and coin hoards dating back 2,500 years, shedding light on early Bengal's trade and civilisation.

name: Ashrafpur Mosque
shortDescription: A 16th-century Sultanate mosque at Ashrafpur village in Shibpur, Narsingdi, a protected monument associated with two famous 7th-century copperplate inscriptions.

name: Daulatdia Ghat
shortDescription: One of Bangladesh's busiest river ferry ports on the Padma river in Rajbari, where large ferries shuttle traffic and vehicles across the river.

name: Baliakandi Rajbari
shortDescription: A 19th-century zamindar mansion at Baliakandi in Rajbari, a historic palace complex with colonial architecture along the Padma river.

name: Haturia Zamindar Bari
shortDescription: A historic zamindar palace at Haturia in Shariatpur, with terracotta-decorated walls and traditional Bengal architecture dating from the colonial period.

name: Mahisar Dighi
shortDescription: A large historic water tank at Mahishar in Bhedarganj, Shariatpur, a revered pilgrimage site for Hindus and a scenic recreation spot surrounded by palm trees.

name: Atia Mosque
shortDescription: A 1609 Sultanate-era mosque at Delduar, Tangail, renowned for its richly decorated terracotta facade and carved stone doorway, a masterpiece of Bengal architecture.

name: Mohera Zamindar Bari
shortDescription: A grand early-20th-century zamindar palace at Mohera, Tangail, blending Mughal and colonial styles, with ornate interiors and a landscaped garden.

name: Dhanbari Nawab Palace
shortDescription: The ornate palace of the Nawabs of Dhanbari in Tangail, a late-19th-century mansion with Mughal-style domes and terracotta work set among gardens.

name: Puthia Rajbari & Temple Complex
shortDescription: A grand 1895 Indo-Saracenic palace surrounded by the largest cluster of historic terracotta Hindu temples in Bangladesh, built by the Puthia Raj zamindar family.
recommendedActivities: Visit the Govinda and Shiva temples

name: Varendra Research Museum
shortDescription: The oldest museum in Bangladesh, founded in 1910, holding a rich collection of archaeological relics, sculptures and manuscripts from ancient Bengal.
recommendedActivities: See the terracotta and stone artefacts
Learn about Pala and Sena period art

name: Bagha Shahi Mosque
shortDescription: A 15th-century single-domed mosque famous for its exquisite terracotta ornamentation, considered among the finest examples of Sultani architecture in Bangladesh.

name: Padma River Bank
shortDescription: A scenic riverfront along the mighty Padma River with promenades, parks and famous mango orchards, popular for sunset views over the water.

name: Shah Makhdum Mazar
shortDescription: The shrine complex of the 14th-century Sufi saint Shah Makhdum, with an octagonal tomb and tank, an important religious and architectural landmark of Rajshahi.

name: Mahasthangarh
shortDescription: The oldest archaeological site in Bangladesh, the ruins of the ancient city of Pundranagara dating back over 2,000 years, with ramparts, temples and artefacts.

name: Gokul Medh
shortDescription: Also known as Behular Bashor Ghar, a small circular Hindu shrine mound associated with the legend of Behula and Lakhindar, beside the Karatoya river.

name: Vasu Vihara
shortDescription: Ruins of an ancient Buddhist monastery near Mahasthangarh dating to the Gupta period, an important seat of learning of early Bengal.

name: Mahasthangarh Archaeological Museum
shortDescription: A museum showcasing coins, sculptures, pottery and ornaments excavated from the ancient city of Pundranagara, narrating over two millennia of history.
recommendedActivities: Short walk to the main site

name: Karatoya River
shortDescription: A sacred river mentioned in ancient texts that once formed the western boundary of Pundravardhana, offering calm boat rides past Mahasthangarh.

name: Shah Sultan Balkhi Mazar
shortDescription: The mausoleum of 10th-century Sufi saint Shah Sultan Balkhi, whose shrine is a major pilgrimage site and one of Bogura's most visited landmarks.

name: Hinda-Kasba Shahi Mosque
shortDescription: A beautiful Mughal-era mosque in Khetlal with fine terracotta decoration, one of the region's notable surviving examples of early mosque architecture.

name: Baro Shib Mondir
shortDescription: A cluster of Shiva temples in Joypurhat town known for their traditional Bengal temple architecture and annual religious fairs.

name: Joypal Rajar Rajbari
shortDescription: Ruins of the ancient palace complex of the legendary king Joypal of Panchbibi, associated with the historic fort city of Garh Kotha.

name: Patisar Kachari Bari
shortDescription: The riverside estate house of Rabindranath Tagore in Patisar, now a museum preserving the poet's family heritage on the banks of the Atrai river.

name: Dubalhati Rajbari
shortDescription: A grand zamindar palace in Dubalhati with a striking facade and central dome, one of the finest colonial-era mansions of northern Bangladesh.

name: Kusumba Mosque
shortDescription: A 16th-century Sultanate-era mosque nicknamed the 'Black Gem of Bengal', richly decorated with stone carvings and terracotta.

name: Balihar Rajbari
shortDescription: A partly-ruined zamindar palace at Balihar known for its elegant arches and columns, a hidden architectural gem of Naogaon.

name: Natore Rajbari
shortDescription: The palace complex of the famous Natore Raj family, known for the legend of Rani Bhabani and elegant royal architecture set amid ponds and gardens.

name: Dighapatia Rajbari (Uttara Ganabhaban)
shortDescription: The historic zamindar palace of Dighapatia, currently the northern official residence of Bangladesh's President, set in beautifully landscaped grounds.

name: Chalan Beel
shortDescription: A vast wetland spanning Natore, Sirajganj and Pabna, a haven for migratory waterbirds with traditional fishing boats and floating villages.

name: Choto Sona Mosque
shortDescription: An exquisite 15th-century Sultanate mosque of dark stone and terracotta, considered one of the finest monuments of the Bengal Sultanate.

name: Darasbari Mosque
shortDescription: The largest Sultanate mosque in the region, built in 1479 with sixty domes, standing among the finest medieval monuments of Bengal.

name: Tahkhana Complex
shortDescription: A 17th-century Mughal complex in Shibganj built by Shah Shuja with a detached palace and mosque, an elegant example of Mughal civic architecture.

name: Khania Dighi Mosque
shortDescription: A 15th-century Sultanate mosque beside a large tank, renowned for its terracotta plaques depicting hunting scenes and daily life.

name: Hardinge Bridge
shortDescription: A 1915 steel railway bridge across the Padma at Paksey, a masterpiece of British colonial engineering with five long spans.

name: Tarash Rajbari
shortDescription: A 19th-century zamindar palace in Pabna town with terracotta ornamentation, one of the last and finest zamindari residences of Bengal.

name: Chatmohar Shahi Mosque
shortDescription: A 1582 Sultanate-era mosque near Chatmohar with an ornamental cornice and fine brickwork, a protected monument of medieval Bengal.

name: Jor Bangla Temple
shortDescription: A traditional two-roofed Jor-Bangla style Hindu temple in Pabna city with fine terracotta panels depicting mythological scenes.

name: Rabindra Kuthibari Shahjadpur
shortDescription: The Kuthibari estate of Rabindranath Tagore at Shahjadpur where the poet stayed and wrote, now a preserved heritage museum.

name: Hatikumrul Navaratna Temple
shortDescription: A rare nine-towered (Navaratna) Hindu temple at Hatikumrul, one of the few surviving examples of this grand Bengal temple style.

name: Shah Mokhdum Mosque
shortDescription: A historic fifteen-domed mosque at Shahjadpur beside the Hurasagar river, an elegant example of medieval Bengal mosque architecture.

name: Hiron Point (Nilkamal)
shortDescription: A prime Sundarbans wildlife-viewing spot where the forest meets the sea, famed for sightings of Royal Bengal tigers, deer and rare birds.
recommendedActivities: Spot Royal Bengal tigers and deer

name: Katka Beach (Tiger Point)
shortDescription: A remote sea beach and watchtower deep in the Sundarbans, offering sweeping views over the Bay of Bengal and the world's largest mangrove forest.

name: Sundarbans Koyra
shortDescription: The Koyra gate of the Sundarbans gives access to serene mangrove creeks, mudflats and villages along the world's largest mangrove ecosystem.

name: Khan Jahan Ali Bridge
shortDescription: A major 2014 road bridge over the Rupsa river connecting Khulna with the south, an important landmark with fine views of the river.

name: Khulna Divisional Museum
shortDescription: A government museum displaying archaeological finds from the Sundarbans region, including sculptures, coins and objects from Khalifatabad.

name: Mausoleum of Khan Jahan Ali
shortDescription: The 1459 tomb complex of the 15th-century Sufi saint Khan Jahan Ali, a UNESCO-listed monument with calligraphic inscriptions beside Thakur Dighi.

name: Nine Dome Mosque
shortDescription: A 15th-century Sultanate mosque with nine domes over a square prayer hall, part of the historic Mosque City of Bagerhat.
recommendedActivities: Combine with the Sixty Dome visit

name: Karamjal Eco-Tourism Center
shortDescription: A Sundarbans eco-tourism center in Mongla with nature trails, deer and monkey enclosures, and the closest easy access point to the mangrove forest.

name: Ghora Dighi
shortDescription: A historic 14th-century tank dug by Khan Jahan Ali's horses, now a scenic lake with cypress-lined banks in Bagerhat town.

name: Three-Domed Bara Mosque
shortDescription: A nearly 250-year-old three-domed mosque in the heart of Chuadanga town, the first mosque built in the district and a living symbol of its heritage.

name: Kalupole Rajar Vita
shortDescription: An excavated archaeological mound at Kalupole, the palace site of King Gandharva Raya with Sultanate-period brick remains on the Chitra river.

name: Sagardari (Madhusudan Memorial)
shortDescription: The ancestral home of poet Michael Madhusudan Dutt at Sagardari, now 'Madhupalli' museum on the banks of the Kapotaksha river.
recommendedActivities: Visit the annual Modhu Mela fair

name: Gadkhali Flower Garden
shortDescription: Sprawling flower gardens in Jhikargacha supplying much of the country's blooms, a colourful patchwork of marigold, rose and jasmine fields.

name: Benapole Land Port
shortDescription: Bangladesh's busiest land port on the India border, a lively hub of cross-border trade, transport and the informal commerce of the frontier.

name: Gorar Mosque
shortDescription: A 15th-century Sultanate mosque near Barobazar with fine terracotta and a rectangular plan, one of the oldest mosques in the region.

name: Naldanga Temple Complex
shortDescription: A cluster of ornate Hindu temples at Naldanga in Kaliganj, including the 'Nau Rath' temple style, decorated with terracotta narratives.

name: Dhol Samudra Dighi
shortDescription: An ancient 18th-century tank in Jhenaidah with an island temple in its middle, surrounded by legend and tranquil waters.

name: Shilaidaha Rabindra Kuthibari
shortDescription: The Kuthibari estate where Rabindranath Tagore lived and wrote many classics, now a museum preserving his memorabilia on the Padma riverbank.

name: Lalon Shah Mazar
shortDescription: The shrine of Baul philosopher Fakir Lalon Shah in Chheuria, a sacred site where followers sing his songs and gather for the annual Lalon Utshab.

name: Lalon Shah Bridge
shortDescription: A 2000 road bridge spanning the Padma between Kushtia and Pabna, a vital transport link with sweeping views of the great river.

name: Raja Sitaram Palace
shortDescription: The 17th-century fort-palace capital of Raja Sitaram Roy at Mohammadpur, with ruins of temples, ponds and the Kachari Bari.

name: Magura Bhater Bhita
shortDescription: A 3rd-century BCE Buddhist structure at Tila village, later used as a mosque and granary, one of the region's oldest archaeological remains.

name: Arpara Eco Park
shortDescription: A green eco-park on the banks of the Nabaganga river at Arpara, a peaceful picnic spot with tree-lined paths and river views.

name: Mujibnagar Memorial
shortDescription: The historic mango grove where Bangladesh's government was sworn in on 17 April 1971, now a grand memorial complex with an archive.

name: Siddheswari Kali Temple
shortDescription: An historic Kali temple in Meherpur town, a revered pilgrimage site with an ancient sanctum and annual worship festivals.

name: Nilkuthi
shortDescription: A surviving colonial indigo factory (Nilkuthi) recalling the oppressive British indigo trade era, an important heritage site of Meherpur.

name: SM Sultan Memorial Museum
shortDescription: The Sultan Complex on the Chitra river preserving the art and tomb of legendary painter SM Sultan, with a gallery of his vivid works.

name: Narail Badha Ghat
shortDescription: A serene water body and ghat beside the Chitra river near Victoria College, a beloved riverside promenade of Narail town.

name: Goal Bathan Mosque
shortDescription: A Mughal-era mosque at Goal Bathan built in 1654, a protected monument with classic brick architecture of the period.

name: Kalagachia Eco-Tourism Center
shortDescription: A Sundarbans eco-tourism center in Shyamnagar with watchtowers, nature trails and mangrove boat rides.

name: Mandarbaria Sea Beach
shortDescription: A wild Sundarbans-adjacent sea beach at Shyamnagar where the mangrove forest meets the Bay of Bengal, popular for sunrise views.

name: Jahajghata Naval Fort
shortDescription: A 16th-century river fort built by Mir Jumla in 1567 to guard against pirates, a historic stronghold of the Arakan era.

name: Sundarbans Satkhira Range
shortDescription: The Satkhira Range of the Sundarbans, accessible from Munshiganj, offering boat safaris through dense mangroves of the world's largest delta forest.

name: Durga Sagar
shortDescription: The largest lake in southern Bangladesh, an 18th-century dighi at Madhabpasha with an island in its centre and winter migratory birds.

name: Guthia Mosque (Baitul Aman)
shortDescription: A dazzling 20-dome marble mosque complex in Wazirpur with a 193-foot minaret, lakes and gardens, one of Bangladesh's most beautiful modern mosques.

name: Kirtankhola River Bank
shortDescription: The winding Kirtankhola river through Barishal city, lined with ghats, parks and the famous floating guava boats, the lifeline of the 'Venice of the East'.

name: Oxford Mission St. Paul's Cathedral
shortDescription: A century-old red-brick cathedral in Barishal, a fine example of Gothic-revival church architecture amid the city's colonial legacy.

name: Qasba Mosque
shortDescription: A 16th-century nine-domed Sultanate mosque at Gournadi, one of the oldest mosques of the greater Barishal region.

name: Laldia Sea Beach
shortDescription: A secluded beach at the confluence of the Baleshwar and Bishkhali rivers, with casuarina forest on one side and the sea on the other.

name: Tengragiri Wildlife Sanctuary
shortDescription: A protected coastal mangrove forest and wildlife sanctuary in Taltali with creeks, deer and birds, a quieter cousin of the Sundarbans.

name: Shuvo Sondha Sea Beach
shortDescription: A four-kilometre sandy beach at the estuary of the Payra, Bishkhali and Baleshwar rivers, backed by casuarina forests in Taltali.

name: Char Kukri-Mukri Wildlife Sanctuary
shortDescription: A remote mangrove island wildlife sanctuary in the Bay of Bengal where the Meghna meets the sea, home to deer, birds and pristine beaches.

name: Tarua Beach
shortDescription: A tranquil beach on Dhal Char in Char Fasson where sunrise and sunset can both be seen, with mangrove forest and waterways around it.

name: Monpura Island
shortDescription: A remote island in the Meghna estuary known for its quiet beaches, fishing villages and the literary fame of 'Aynabaji' and monsoon beauty.

name: Fatima Digital Museum
shortDescription: Bangladesh's first digital museum in Bhola town, an innovative interactive exhibition of local history and the Liberation War.

name: Bhimruli Floating Guava Market
shortDescription: During guava season, farmers trade fresh fruit from wooden boats on the canal at Bhimruli, one of Bangladesh's most iconic floating markets.

name: Kirtipasha Zamindar Bari
shortDescription: Ruins of the grand Kirtipasha zamindar estate built by Ramjibon Sen, with a Shiva temple and remnants of a once-magnificent palace.

name: Gabkhan Bridge
shortDescription: A high S-shaped bridge over the Gabkhan channel west of Jhalokathi town, offering elevated views over the busy waterways of the delta.

name: Gangamati Reserved Forest
shortDescription: A protected coastal forest near Kuakata with native trees and birdlife, offering quiet nature walks and shoreline views.

name: Mishripara Seema Buddha Bihar

Walk the zoo and aviary sections
